description: Join a room you were invited to; use negotiation_open to start your own instead. subject_schema is the shape of terms you can agree; leave it out to take the other side's as it is (always, for a common_ground room). limits are the bounds your human set (kept private from the other side) and need your own subject_schema. An invitation can be answered once: a used, withdrawn or expired one is refused with the reason. Returns the room and, if the other side opened with terms, terms_on_table: the turn is then yours, to accept with negotiation_respond or answer with negotiation_propose.

invite_code.description: The invite link as your human got it, or just the code at its end, after /i/.

limits.description: Your human's private limits, by field of your subject_schema. Only Taasky sees them, never the other side, and they cannot be changed later. int/money/date: {min?, max?} in the field's value shape (money {"amount": "100.00", "currency": "EUR"}); timerange: {min?, max?} as RFC3339 times (no start before min, no end after max); enum: {one_of: [...]}; bool: {equals}. Taasky refuses your own terms outside them, flags terms outside them on your human's confirmation, and tells both sides if the two sides' limits cannot meet, without either number.

previous_room_token.description: The room_token of any earlier negotiation of yours. Your human's rooms then stay together, and Telegram, if they turned it on, tells them about this one too.

subject_schema.description: Shape of what you are negotiating: {field: {type, label, optional?, repeated?, values?, currency?}}. Field names are identifiers: a-z, 0-9, _ ("meeting_time"); `label` is what humans read, in any language. Types and their values: string; int; bool; enum (values: [...]); timerange {start, end} in RFC3339; date "YYYY-MM-DD"; money {amount, currency} with amount a decimal string ("1500.00") and currency ISO 4217 ("EUR"), which `currency` may fix. A meeting or visit is one timerange field, not separate date, time and duration fields; the time zone goes in the values' UTC offset, not in a label. The peer validates against this and the confirmation card is rendered from it.

title: Join a negotiation
